edges.description: The authors of the fusion studies conclude that at least a large subset of simple bone cysts are cystic neoplasms defined by the fusion. The edge records that reading as a hypothesis. What the studies show is that the fusion is present in the lesion; none shows a step that leads from the fusion to a fluid-filled cavity, so the link is typed as indirect with unknown intermediates and its evidence as indirect.

Venous obstruction is proposed as the cause of the cyst. The proposal rests on pressure and oxygen measurements in existing cysts, which cannot show what came first, and on the results of decompression. How an obstruction would start the cavity is not shown.
edges.source: Venous Outflow Obstruction and Raised Intracystic Pressure

edges.description: A 2026 review joins the two older observations into one chain: the obstruction may raise the pressure in the cyst and let fluid rich in proteolytic enzymes and prostaglandins accumulate, which then degrades bone matrix. The review words this as a possibility, and no study cited here tests the chain.

edges.description: Resorption of the surrounding bone is proposed to enlarge the cavity and thin its wall. The claim is the authors' reading of what they found in the fluid; the resorption itself was not measured. The edge is placed in the venous-obstruction hypothesis because the 2024 review that states that account names enzymatic lysis in the same sentence as venous obstruction. That sentence is quoted under the hypothesis.

nodes.description: The fluid of the cyst carries factors that resorb bone. A 2012 study of the fluid of two cysts found three cytokines that promote osteoclast formation highly raised, and osteoclasts in abundance in the cyst lining.

nodes.description: Injection of methylprednisolone acetate into the cyst, repeated until the cyst heals. In the one randomised trial, 16 of 38 cysts had healed at two years, against 9 of 39 after bone marrow injection; the trial calls the healing rate low in both arms, and a Cochrane review rates the evidence as very low in quality. A meta-analysis of retrospective studies gives a pooled healing rate of 77.4 per cent. A 2024 review says the treatment is now used less, because of the repeated injections and the fractures that occur before healing. Why a steroid should work has not been shown.

nodes.description: Open removal of the lining of the cyst, with filling of the cavity by bone graft or bone substitute. A meta-analysis of retrospective studies gives a healing rate of 90 per cent with autograft or allograft. Recurrence is the concern: 5 of 13 cysts recurred after curettage and bone substitute in one series, and of 106 children treated by surgery, 17 had recurred and 13 had not responded at 12 months. For cysts of the calcaneus, a systematic review found that 93.0 per cent had healed after surgery and 1.1 per cent under conservative treatment.

nodes.description: A fusion of FUS or EWSR1 with NFATC2 is found in a large proportion of simple bone cysts of the long bones and pelvis. The first study found one in 7 of 11 cysts (six by RNA sequencing and one more by other methods). Later series found an NFATC2 fusion in 7 of 11 and in 6 of 9 cysts, an EWSR1-NFATC2 fusion in 3 of 9 with a FUS rearrangement in a fourth, and an EWSR1 or FUS rearrangement in 9 of 14. In the cysts the fusion is not amplified, which separates them from the round cell sarcomas that carry the same fusion. Nine cysts of the jaw that could be tested all lacked an NFATC2 rearrangement. The studies cited do not say which cell of the cyst wall carries the fusion, and none shows how the fusion would produce a cyst.

nodes.description: The older account of the cyst. In a 1983 study the pressure inside the cysts was slightly higher than the marrow pressure in the opposite limb, it fell as drill holes were made, and the oxygen tension of the cyst fluid was markedly lower than that of venous or arterial blood; the authors suggested that venous obstruction in the bone is the likely cause. Reviews still give this account: one states that high intraosseous pressure caused by venous obstruction, with enzymatic lysis, is considered responsible for the cyst, and another calls impaired venous drainage of the metaphysis a particularly compelling hypothesis. What obstructs the veins is not known.
